added_failures_note: unmeasured, not zero: the reviewed manifest records baseline_suite and after_suite as 'not run - the write paths reach no test path other than the node's own new unit test, so no repository suite covers this change', so both arms are absent and added_failures_from_gate_logs returns (None, []) for the pair (reckon/crew/review.py:2136).

findings.text: the sentence 'The one measured quantity that does differ between the arms across the bracket is the booked current jump at the fold: 7.438e-15 per target at base against 3.402e-3 at head' attributes the superseded head's number to the restored head. The restored receipts are identical at both arms: restore-sweep-diverted-250-{base,head}.json both carry raw_current_jump_per_target 7.437515551812588e-15 and restore-sweep-diverted-500-{base,head}.json both carry 5.284562381285093e-15, and every one of the 41 per-state rows agrees field for field between the arms on all four sweep receipts (offset, boundary_flux, wall_candidate, saddle_candidate, boundary_class, raw_current: zero differences). The 0.0034016909292876305 value exists only in fix-sweep-diverted-250-head.json, the earlier arm of the withdrawn scope that job 1288113 produced before the membership was restored. So the record states a base/head divergence that the restored pair does not have, in the one paragraph that admits a difference between the arms, directly against the node's own headline that the head is base to the last printed digit. A reader of this record concludes the restoration is incomplete when it is exact.

the continuity assertion's expected value is the same expression the test hands in as the tangency operand, and np.allclose's default rtol=1e-5 tolerates the 1e-6 mismatch that a true minimum produces here, so the assertion does not assert the continuity it names. swept = _wall_effective_level(0.5 + linspace(-1e-6, 1e-6, 5), full((5,), 0.5)) evaluates to [0.499999, 0.4999995, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5] under the landed minimum, while the expectation 0.5 + linspace(-1e-6, 1e-6, 5) is [0.499999, 0.4999995, 0.5, 0.5000005, 0.500001]; the last two entries differ by 5e-7 and 1e-6 against a tolerance of 1e-8 + 1e-5*0.5 = 5e-6, so it passes on an implementation that clamps above 0.5, and it also passes unchanged for an identity function (exact match) and for a maximum (differences of the same 5e-7/1e-6 magnitude, both inside tolerance). The test's load-bearing assertions are the ones above it - test_private_flux_contact_takes_the_saddle_level:130 and the first allclose at :146 both redden if the minimum becomes a maximum - so the file does pin the landed behaviour; only this line's stated guarantee is unsupported.

justifications.durability: scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/test_bottleneck_level.py:130 fails if _wall_effective_level stops taking the more scrape-off-side of the two operands (a maximum returns -0.05 where the test asserts -0.5 against an independently authored saddle level), and :146 pins the same function against three authored expectations; docked five because the continuity assertion at :152 compares the output against the input expression it was handed and passes under np.allclose defaults for the minimum, an identity and a maximum alike, so it does not carry the guarantee its name and the research page claim for it (docs/research/bottleneck-path-level.html:143 'asserts the effective level moves with it, so the rule is continuous in both operands with no step').
justifications.evidence: the gate is recorded rather than claimed and I read the receipts: logs/unit-test.log names revision fc8cfd1f7 and ends '2 passed in 10.81s / EXIT=0', and the eight fidelity rows and four sweep rows in restore-*.json reproduce base to the last printed digit at both arms, which I re-derived from the files (zero field differences across all 41 states of each sweep); docked six because no repository suite was run at either arm so added_failure_count is unmeasured, because the 2,098-cell row the dispatched clause 3 named is unmeasured, and because docs/research/bottleneck-path-level.html:106 records a base/head difference at the fold that the restored receipts do not show.

justifications.goal_fidelity: the landed change delivers the corrected deliverable - scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/kernel.py:120 names the wall contact's effective level as one owned function called from the wall-score site at :299, and the record measures that the read is otherwise unchanged - but it does not produce the dispatched goal ('replace the fast map 0/1 axis-path membership'), because the coordinator withdrew the replacement in resume-3 and the node instead restored membership and reported base as already correct; docked four because a reader holding only the dispatched goal and this diff finds no replacement in it.
justifications.reuse: the added definition extends the owner of its capability rather than forking it: the minimum it names lived inline in scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/kernel.py:287 at the orientation revision, and the change moves that expression into the module that already owns the topology read; a capability search over nova/ and scripts/ for an existing 'effective level' or 'more scrape-off-side of tangency and bottleneck' owner returned only the sibling prototype scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production and scripts/prototypes/diverted_stall/kernel.py:177, a separate prototype the node did not touch and did not duplicate; docked one because that sibling still carries the same inline minimum, so the rule is now named in one module and inline in another.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is inside the node's declared write paths - scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/kernel.py and its new test, docs/research/bottleneck-path-level.html, docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/bottleneck-path-level.html, and the two SVGs under docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/bottleneck-path-level - and the code change carries nothing the corrected goal does not imply; docked two because the manifest's changed_paths list omits docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/bottleneck-path-level/bottleneck-level-bracket.svg, which the head commit fc8cfd1f7 added.
